items.title: Show & Tell: Windows Desktop Shell + WSL Backend, Cross-Compiled from Linux ★

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## What We Built

A native Windows **Hermes Desktop** shell that connects to a WSL2 backend — with zero Hermes installation on Windows. Cross-compiled the Electron app on Linux, pointed it at WSL via `HERMES_DESKTOP_REMOTE_URL`.

### Architecture

```
Windows Desktop  →  Hermes.exe (native, cross-compiled from WSL/Linux)
     ↓ localhost:9120
WSL2             →  hermes dashboard + gateway (single default profile, includes WeChat bot)
```

### Key Hacks & Learnings

**1. Electron Download — 30x Speedup**
- npm/node HTTP stack: **67 KB/s** through proxy
- `curl` direct: **3.2 MB/s**
- Pre-downloaded Electron zip, used `ELECTRON_OVERRIDE_DIST_PATH` to skip npm download
- 110MB file: 35 seconds vs 30+ minutes

**2. Cross-Compile Windows Exe from Linux**
- `npx electron-builder --win --x64 --dir` works from WSL
- Produces valid `win-unpacked/Hermes.exe` (PE32+)
- Requires `ELECTRON_SKIP_BINARY_DOWNLOAD=1` to avoid redundant download

**3. Session Token Auth**
- Desktop env mode uses `X-Hermes-Session-Token` header, NOT basic auth
- Must set `HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN` on dashboard
- Token passed via `HERMES_DESKTOP_REMOTE_TOKEN` env var to desktop
- `api_server` platform needs `API_SERVER_KEY` set

**4. Profile Consolidation**
- Desktop app needs dashboard + gateway in same profile
- Moved WeChat bot config from weixin → default profile
- Single gateway serves both api_server + weixin platforms

**5. Windows Batch File Gotcha**
- `.bat` files must use CRLF, not LF
- Chinese filenames get garbled on Windows when written from WSL
- PowerShell base64 decoding for token avoids special character issues

### Result
Native Windows Hermes window, WSL backend, WeChat bot uninterrupted. No Windows Hermes installation required.

### Versions
- Hermes Agent v0.16.0 (d986bb0c)
- Electron v40.9.3  
- electron-builder v26.8.1
- WSL2 with WSLg

### Summary
An attacker operating as **jellyfinuser** on gitea.com has created three public repositories containing malware targeting Hermes Agent instances. These plugins exploit the `--insecure` dashboard flag and Hermes' auto-loading plugin system to gain remote shell access and deploy SSH backdoors.

3. Hermes plugin auto-loader picks it up on dashboard restart

5. The hermes plugin can optionally deploy attacker's SSH key to authorized_keys

- Full root access to servers running Hermes dashboard with --insecure

items.title: Honcho: injected skill invocation text syncs to memory as user speech, polluting the deriver

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

When a skill is invoked, Hermes builds a user-role message containing the activation note plus the **full skill content** (agent/skill_commands.py `_build_skill_message`, also cron/scheduler.py and agent/skill_bundles.py):

```
[IMPORTANT: The user has invoked the "<skill>" skill, indicating they want you to follow its instructions. The full skill content is loaded below.]
<entire SKILL.md content...>
```

The Honcho plugin's `_flush_session` (plugins/memory/honcho/session.py) syncs every user-role message to Honcho verbatim with no filtering, so multi-KB skill instruction dumps are stored as things the *user said*.

## Impact

Honcho's deriver attributes the skill's instructions to the user and derives "facts" from them. On a single-user deployment we measured 300+ conclusions of the form:

- "sam's 'capture' skill requires appending a one-line ingest event to CORPUS_LOG.md"
- "sam's capture workflow includes routing rules directing full conversation handoff to transcript logs"

These pollute peer cards and compete with real user facts in dialectic retrieval.

## Expected

Framework-injected scaffolding (skill activations, preloaded skill prompts) should be excluded from memory provider sync — it isn't user speech and isn't a durable fact about the user. A flag on synthetic messages (e.g. `synthetic: true` checked in `_flush_session`), or skipping messages with the known activation prefix, would cover it.

## Workaround

Reverse proxy between Hermes and Honcho dropping messages whose content starts with `[IMPORTANT: The user has invoked`.

Related: #43731 (memory file migration re-runs per session — the other major deriver noise source).

items.title: [Bug]: openai-codex credential pool marks healthy later account as usage_limit_reached; auth reset restores operation

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
### Bug Description

# Summary

Hermes incorrectly marked all openai-codex pooled credentials as rate-limited, including a third account that still had available quota according to ChatGPT /backend-api/wham/usage.

After running:

hermes auth reset openai-codex

Hermes immediately resumed working and selected the third credential successfully.

This suggests a stale or incorrectly assigned exhaustion state in the openai-codex credential pool.

Environment

Hermes Agent v0.16.0 (2026.6.5)
upstream: 4cecb1a1
Python: 3.11.15
OpenAI SDK: 2.24.0
Provider: openai-codex
Model: gpt-5.5
Credential pool strategy: fill_first

Config excerpt:

model:
  provider: openai-codex
fallback_providers: []
credential_pool_strategies:
  openai-codex: fill_first
agent:
  api_max_retries: 3


Additional diagnostics

Token fingerprints showed that the singleton provider state matched pool entry #1, not #3:

providers.openai-codex.tokens.access_fp == pool #1 access_fp
pool #3 access_fp was different

So the issue does not appear to be simply that pool #3 was overwritten by the singleton provider token.

Suspected cause

The local code path appears to persist provider reset timestamps into the pool entry:

last_error_reset_at = normalized_error.get("reset_at")

and _normalize_error_context() accepts resets_at, reset_at, or retry_until.

The recovery path calls:

pool.mark_exhausted_and_rotate(status_code=rotate_status, error_context=error_context)

without passing an api_key_hint.

However, mark_exhausted_and_rotate() supports api_key_hint and otherwise falls back to:

entry = self.current() or self._select_unlocked()

This may allow Hermes to mark the current pool entry as exhausted even if the actual failed HTTP request was sent using a stale runtime client/token from a previous credential.

If that happens, a healthy later credential can be marked as usage_limit_reached, and because the upstream error includes a long resets_at, the healthy credential remains locally blocked until hermes auth reset openai-codex is run.



### Steps to Reproduce

Credential pool state before reset

openai-codex (3 credentials):
  #1  device_code          oauth   device_code rate-limited usage_limit_reached (429) (1d 3h left)
  #2  openai-codex-oauth-2 oauth   device_code rate-limited usage_limit_reached (429) (5d 0h left)
  #3  openai-codex-oauth-3 oauth   device_code rate-limited usage_limit_reached (429) (29d 20h left)

The third account was expected to still be usable. A direct wham/usage request using the third account’s token showed:

{
  "plan_type": "plus",
  "rate_limit": {
    "allowed": true,
    "limit_reached": false,
    "primary_window": {
      "used_percent": 45
    },
    "secondary_window": {
      "used_percent": 7
    }
  },
  "rate_limit_reached_type": null
}

Runtime symptom

A fresh minimal CLI call failed with usage_limit_reached even though the third account still had quota:

hermes chat --provider openai-codex --model gpt-5.5 -q "Answer exactly with: OK"

Output:

API call failed (attempt 1/3): RateLimitError [HTTP 429]
Provider: openai-codex
Model: gpt-5.5
Endpoint: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex
Error: HTTP 429: The usage limit has been reached
Details: {'type': 'usage_limit_reached', 'message': 'The usage limit has been reached', 'plan_type': 'plus', 'resets_at': 1781216556, ...}
Context: 2 msgs, ~6,614 tokens

Gateway logs showed the same error:

WARNING agent.conversation_loop: API call failed ... provider=openai-codex base_url=https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex model=gpt-5.5 summary=HTTP 429: The usage limit has been reached
ERROR agent.conversation_loop: API call failed after 3 retries. HTTP 429: The usage limit has been reached | provider=openai-codex model=gpt-5.5

Workaround

Running:

hermes auth reset openai-codex

produced:

Reset status on 3 openai-codex credentials

After that, the same minimal call succeeded:

hermes chat --provider openai-codex --model gpt-5.5 -q "Answer exactly with: OK"

Output:

OK

The pool state afterwards was correct:

openai-codex (3 credentials):
  #1  device_code          oauth   device_code rate-limited usage_limit_reached (429) (1d 3h left)
  #2  openai-codex-oauth-2 oauth   device_code rate-limited usage_limit_reached (429) (5d 0h left)
  #3  openai-codex-oauth-3 oauth   device_code ←

### Expected Behavior

For openai-codex credential pools:

1. A usage_limit_reached response should mark only the credential that actually sent the failed HTTP request.
2. A healthy later credential should not be marked exhausted due to a stale/current pointer mismatch.
3. The recovery path should pass the actual failed credential identity/token/key into mark_exhausted_and_rotate(api_key_hint=...), or otherwise ensure the runtime client and pool.current() cannot diverge.
4. auth reset should not be required to recover a still-valid pooled credential.

including a third account whose direct usage endpoint still reported:

allowed=true
limit_reached=false

This can make Hermes unusable with openai-codex multi-account pools even when a later account still has quota. The user-visible error is a misleading rate-limit failure until hermes auth reset openai-codex is manually run.

Proposed fix direction

Specifically, the openai-codex recovery path should avoid marking pool.current() unless it can prove that pool.current() is the credential used by the HTTP request that returned 429.

## Feature Request: Auto-TTS Mode on Desktop

**The problem:** The desktop app currently has no way to automatically speak every assistant response via TTS while keeping keyboard/text as the input method.

The CLI/TUI supports this via `/voice tts` (type your input, hear responses spoken aloud) — but the desktop app blocks the `/voice` slash command and instead offers:
- **Voice Conversation** (mic → STT → agent → TTS) — full duplex, but uses microphone for input
- **Read Aloud** (right-click per-message) — manual, not automatic
- **Dictation** (speech-to-text only)

There is no "keyboard input + auto-TTS output" mode.

**Desired behavior:** A toggle (in the composer toolbar and/or settings) that auto-reads every new assistant response aloud via TTS, while keeping the text input field as the primary input method. The existing `playSpeechText` / `ReadAloudItem` components already do the heavy lifting — it just needs a persistent flag that triggers `playSpeechText(source: 'read-aloud')` on each new message automatically.

**Suggested implementation approach:**
- A toggle button in the composer area (e.g., a speaker icon that highlights when active)
- A persistent setting in `config.yaml` / desktop settings
- When active, each new assistant message triggers the same TTS path as the existing Read Aloud button, but automatically
- Streaming TTS (sentence-by-sentence) would be ideal, matching the CLI behaviour
- User can still type normally in the composer — no mic/VAD involved

**Additional context:** The voice playback infrastructure already exists — `voice-playback.ts`, `source: 'read-aloud'`, `ReadAloudItem`, `VoicePlaybackActivity`. This is essentially wiring a persistent auto-read flag into the message-received flow.

## Problem

Accessing Google Calendar for delegated users (Christie, Claudia) via the --user flag fails with **HttpError 403: accessNotConfigured**. The Google Calendar API has not been used in project 391162310014 before or it is disabled.

Chris primary calendar works fine (direct OAuth token). Only delegated access via service account is broken.

## Root Cause

The Google Calendar API is **not enabled** in GCP project 391162310014 (the project used for service account email-sync@email-ingestion-480518.iam.gserviceaccount.com). The service account was originally set up for email-only delegation. Calendar API was never enabled for it.

## What Needs to Be Done

1. **Enable Google Calendar API** in GCP project 391162310014:
   - Visit https://console.developers.google.com/apis/api/calendar-json.googleapis.com/overview?project=391162310014
   - Click Enable

2. **Add Calendar scope to domain-wide delegation** in Google Admin Console:
   - Google Admin Console > Security > Access and data control > API controls > Domain-wide delegation
   - Edit the service account entry for email-sync@email-ingestion-480518.iam.gserviceaccount.com
   - Add https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar to the OAuth scope list

3. **Verify** delegation works after changes:
   - Run google_api.py --user christie@chrishamptonlaw.com calendar list --max 1

## Affected Skill

google-workspace skill -- --user flag for domain-wide delegation

items.title: google-workspace skill: domain-wide delegation scopes need audit and documentation
items.body:
## Problem

The google-workspace skill supports domain-wide delegation via --user flag to access other users mailboxes, calendars, etc. However, scopes are split between two configurations that can easily drift out of sync:

- **OAuth scopes** in setup.py / google_api.py SCOPES list (Chris direct token)
- **DELEGATED_SCOPES** in google_api.py (service account delegation)
- **Google Admin Console** authorized scopes (what the service account is actually allowed to use)
- **GCP project APIs** enabled (what APIs the OAuth client can call)

When any of these four layers are out of sync, delegated access silently fails with cryptic errors (403 accessNotConfigured, unauthorized_client, etc.)

## Specific Issue Discovered

Calendar API worked for Chris (direct OAuth) but failed for delegated users because:
1. Calendar API was never enabled in the GCP project
2. Calendar scope was never added to Admin Console delegation

The error message was confusing: "Google Calendar API has not been used in project X before or it is disabled"

## Proposed Improvements

1. **Scope diagnostic command** — Add a --scope-check flag to google_api.py or setup.py that:
   - Compares SCOPES vs DELEGATED_SCOPES
   - Tests each delegated scope by making a minimal API call
   - Reports which scopes work and which fail, with actionable fix URLs

2. **Documentation** — Add a troubleshooting section to the google-workspace skill SKILL.md:
   - Explain the four-layer scope system (OAuth, DELEGATED_SCOPES, Admin Console, GCP APIs)
   - Map common errors to their root causes and fixes
   - Include the GCP API enable URLs for each scope (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Sheets, Docs, Contacts)

3. **DELEGATED_SCOPES vs SCOPES sync check** — Warn at startup if DELEGATED_SCOPES references scopes not in SCOPES or vice versa

items.title: [Bug]: Honcho memory plugin silently fails against self-hosted Honcho v3.x server (honcho-ai SDK pinned to v2)
items.body:
### Bug Description

The Honcho memory plugin is pinned to honcho-ai==2.0.1 in pyproject.toml, but the current self-hosted Honcho Docker image ships server v3.x. The v2 SDK's Honcho(workspace=...) constructor is rejected by the v3 server's pydantic validator, so every Honcho instance fails to construct.

The plugin's fail-open startup path swallows the construction error. The four honcho_* tools (honcho_profile, honcho_search, honcho_reasoning, honcho_conclude) all return empty results, and there is no log-level signal that anything is broken unless logging.level=DEBUG is set.

End result: the Honcho integration appears to be working — no errors are surfaced to the user — but every memory read/write is silently dropped. The user has no way to know their self-hosted Honcho container is unreachable from Hermes's perspective.

This breaks the integration for all users on a current self-hosted Honcho install — anyone who pulled the Docker image after the v3 release is affected, not just users on a custom config.

Related: #43731, #43733 (both observed on self-hosted Honcho deployments).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Spin up the current self-hosted Honcho Docker stack (honcho-ai/honcho:latest, or any v3.x tag). Confirm /health returns {"status":"ok"} and /openapi.json reports version: 3.x.x.
2. Configure Hermes with memory.provider: honcho in ~/.hermes/config.yaml and set HONCHO_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8500 (or your container's mapped port).
3. Confirm ~/.honcho/config.json is populated: peer, workspace, endpoint.baseUrl.
4. From any Hermes session, invoke honcho_profile (or any of the other three honcho_* tools).
5. Observe: tool returns "No result from Honcho." with no error surfaced to the caller.
6. With logging.level=DEBUG, observe the underlying pydantic validation error during plugin init:
`pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for Honcho.__init__
workspace
  Unexpected keyword argument [type=unexpected_keyword_argument, input_value='personal', input_type=str]`

### Expected Behavior

The plugin should successfully construct against the current self-hosted Honcho server (v3.x), with the honcho-ai SDK pin updated to match the v3 server's API.

If the plugin cannot construct (e.g. a version skew we don't yet handle), it should log a clear logger.error() with the version mismatch and the remediation, and return an explicit error from the honcho_* tools rather than returning empty results with no signal.

The current behavior — silent emptiness on every read and write — is the worst-of-both-worlds failure mode: the user believes the integration is working and has no way to discover it isn't.

### Actual Behavior

Every honcho_* tool call returns "No result from Honcho" or "Failed to save conclusion" with no error surfaced to the caller. The plugin appears to be working from the user's perspective: no error banner, no status indicator, no warning at startup.

Underlying error (visible only at DEBUG log level during plugin initialization):
`pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for Honcho.__init__
workspace
  Unexpected keyword argument [type=unexpected_keyword_argument, input_value='personal', input_type=str]
    For further information visit https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.13/v/unexpected_keyword_argument`

The error comes from the v2 SDK's pydantic validator rejecting the workspace= keyword that the plugin passes to Honcho(...). The keyword signature changed between SDK v2 and v3.

### Affected Component

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
Report paste.rs/oGgJ5 
agent.log paste.rs/ukaLU 
desktop.log paste.rs/6otx9
```

### Operating System

macOS 26.5

### Python Version

3.11

### Hermes Version

0.16.0

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

Three things are misaligned:

pyproject.toml pins honcho-ai==2.0.1 — exact pin, not a range. The v2 SDK is the only version that can construct.

The self-hosted Honcho Docker image is at server 3.0.9 (verified via /openapi.json on http://localhost:8500/openapi.json → "version": "3.0.9"). The v3 server's API surface moved to /v3/... paths; the v2 SDK's Honcho client targets v2 paths and pydantic-validates differently.

plugins/memory/honcho/client.py constructs Honcho(workspace=...) with a v2-style keyword signature. When the v2 SDK is forced to talk to the v3 server (because that's all the user has installed), the SDK's pydantic validator rejects the constructor call before any HTTP is attempted. The plugin's init path catches this as a generic exception and returns None / empty, leaving the tools to fail-open.

The fix surface is:

Bump the honcho-ai pin to >=3.0 in pyproject.toml
Update plugins/memory/honcho/client.py to use the v3 SDK's constructor signature and call paths
Keep migrate_memory_files() and _flush_session() behavior unchanged so the workarounds described in #43731 and #43733 (reverse-proxy filtering) remain valid

### Proposed Fix (optional)

1. In pyproject.toml:
`- honcho = ["honcho-ai==2.0.1"]
+ honcho = ["honcho-ai>=3.0,<4.0"]`

2.  In plugins/memory/honcho/client.py, migrate from the v2 SDK's Honcho(workspace=...) signature to the v3 SDK's constructor (signature change is the proximate cause; full v3 surface migration is the rest of the work). Exact rewrite needs to be validated against the v3 SDK's actual API, which is what the PR will demonstrate.

I'm planning to open a PR for this. Will reference this issue in the PR description.
